hero.lede: An inter-university project that uses design thinking as a new way to teach.

films.search: Search a film, a team or a school

paras: Rails of Time is an inter-university project that applies design thinking to how teaching is designed.

The title is a play on words: "Rails of Time" is both a real route and a link between generations, cultures and traditions. Traveling from one French city to the next, participants find traces of past and present culture and meet the people whose creativity shapes each region.

The project works like a modern travel journal. Students plan the itineraries, make short films, conduct interviews and write up their research, and along the way they get to know the local culture and the people who innovate and create there.

items.p: Turn students’ coursework into real fieldwork with towns, companies and local organizations across France.
Build interviewing, filmmaking and intercultural skills by documenting real local “heroes.”
Show how communities and businesses of every size drive cultural, economic and ecological change.
Have Generation U students mentor younger pupils and share their work with the public.

outline.lede: The project runs in stages, each building on the last: students create first, then pass on what they have learned to younger pupils.

phases.label: Phase 1
phases.p: This first stage is for students at our partner universities and schools. It is built into their coursework.
phases.quote: Local companies and figures become the "heroes" of the students' films and the subject of their academic work.

phases.label: Phase 2
phases.p: This stage is about passing knowledge from one generation to the next. University students become tutors and mentors for middle and high school pupils and guide them through the whole project.

cta.p: Join our creative and educational projects, or get in touch to talk about becoming a partner.

hero.lede: When cultures meet, they change us and the world around us.

paras: ASSO S.L.A.V.É. is an intellectual laboratory where people from all walks of life work together on creative, educational and sustainable projects.

The association's main work is building projects that combine science, entrepreneurship, culture, art, sustainable development and technology. It pays particular attention to cinema, digital media and artificial intelligence, and to traditional art forms, which it uses as tools for intercultural exchange and responsible development.
about.caption: The S.L.A.V.É. Bordeaux team

history.title: History & Values
history.hint: Founded in 2007 at Université Bordeaux Montaigne. How the association got here.
paras: The association was founded in 2007 at Université Bordeaux Montaigne by students and professors passionate about cultural dialogue with Eastern Europe, former USSR countries, and the Slavic world.

From the start, the association organized many cultural and scientific events, led by professionals from business, academia and the arts. One of its best-known projects was In Ciné Veritas, an international short film competition.

Over time it grew and became more structured, adding teaching workshops in communication, management, entrepreneurship, art, the creative industries and marketing. It also offers interpreting and written translation, in keeping with its academic origins.

This work draws on action research and design thinking. It extends into creative projects, tourism routes in France and Europe, and the promotion of local areas and their businesses, whatever their size.

The association also works for inclusion and respect for human dignity. Its projects open up culture, education and creative work to many different audiences, and encourage people to take part, act independently and express themselves, which it sees as the basis of responsible, sustainable development.
Today the association reaches well beyond its original scope. It works across disciplines, generations and cultures, locally and at European level.
It has stayed true to its academic roots and to its belief that education, culture and art are tools for change.

pillars.lede: Five fields through which the association brings cultures together.

items.p: Educational workshops and academic projects in management, entrepreneurship, applied linguistics, AI and the creative industries.
Translation, interpretation and intercultural mediation that bring people, institutions and cultures together.
Cinema, digital media and audiovisual creation, with a special focus on film and new technologies.
Cultural and tourism routes to meet the people and places that shape France’s regions.
Mobility, inclusion and exchange, so that people and communities from different backgrounds meet and share experiences.

featured.lede: Our two main projects: one about culture and education, one about solidarity.

img.alt: Students filming an interview for their Rails of Time short film

items.p: An intercultural and educational journey across France. Students design routes, make short documentary films and tell the stories of the people who shape each region.
Social action and intercultural support for individuals and families: translation, guidance and help building community ties, with respect for each person's dignity.

hero.lede: The association runs practical actions and long-term projects to support individuals and families, strengthen community ties and promote everyone's dignity.

items.p: Solidarity and support for older people, children and families.
Help newcomers settle in, with information, translation and interpreting.
Link generations through workshops, shared activities and a community library.
Help with respect for privacy and dignity, never replacing qualified professionals.

areas.lede: Regular, one-off and on-the-ground help for people in need

bullets: Help with moving within the care facility

items.p: Growing together and opening up new possibilities.
bullets: Support for family projects and initiatives
Books and resources to find information, learn and get inspired
Films and documentaries to discover and borrow
A space for exchange and ongoing learning

furniture.lede: Light repairs and restoration of furniture for elderly residents: a practical way of caring for people and their dignity.

items.p: Bringing young volunteers and elderly people together through shared activities.
Building a tailored career path with each person.
bullets: Adapted career paths (e.g., PE teacher turned tiler, foreign diploma validation via ENIC-NARIC)
CV and cover letter writing workshops
Connection with training centers (AFPA, CNAM) and integration structures

paras: Our work is done by volunteers, on an occasional and time-limited basis.
We help people with their paperwork (translation, guidance) and with planning and developing their own projects.
We work within the limits of our skills and resources and never replace qualified professionals (legal, medical or social).
We keep strictly to these limits and respect the privacy and independence of the people we support.

cta.p: Join us as a volunteer, a partner or a donor. Write to us and we will tell you how you can help.
